extraction.name: CONTEXTUAL
extraction.description: CONTEXTUAL is a novel dataset featuring human-crafted instructions that require context-sensitive reasoning for text-rich images. It consists of 506 challenging instructions for large multimodal model (LMM) evaluation, covering eight real-world scenarios: time reading, shopping, navigation, abstract scenes, mobile application, webpages, infographics, and miscellaneous natural scenes. Each instance contains a human-written instruction and a human-written ground-truth response, with the constraint that accurately responding requires context-sensitive joint reasoning over textual and visual cues in the image.
extraction.creator: Rohan Wadhawan, Hritik Bansal, Kai-Wei Chang, Nanyun Peng (University of California Los Angeles)
extraction.citeAs: Wadhawan, R., Bansal, H., Chang, K.-W., & Peng, N. (2024). CONTEXTUAL: Evaluating Context-Sensitive Text-Rich Visual Reasoning in Large Multimodal Models. Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, Vienna, Austria. PMLR 235.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were sourced from six different sources: LAION-5B (for Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract categories via keyword search using CLIP-retrieval UI), the Rico Dataset (for Application Usage), screenshots scraped from Open WebText Initiative website links (for Web Usage), and test sets of existing VQA datasets (InfographicVQA for Infographic category; STVQA and ESTVQA for Miscellaneous Natural Scenes). Human-written instruction-response pairs were then annotated by the authors following collection guidelines, with verification by Amazon Mechanical Turk workers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web API
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images sourced from: (1) LAION-5B via CLIP-retrieval UI keyword search for Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract categories; (2) Rico Dataset (66,000 distinct UI screens from 9,300 Android apps) for Application Usage; (3) Screenshots from Open WebText Initiative website links for Web Usage; (4) InfographicVQA dataset test set for Infographic; (5) STVQA and ESTVQA dataset test sets for Miscellaneous Natural Scenes.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For Application Usage, Web Usage, Infographic, and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes categories, heuristic-based filtering was applied using PaddleOCR to detect text in images, selecting the top 500 images with the highest number of words. For Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract categories, manual filtering was performed to guarantee suitability for annotation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Stage 1: Images were shortlisted via manual filtering (for Time, Shopping, Navigation, Abstract) or heuristic-based filtering using PaddleOCR to select top 500 images with the highest word count (for Application Usage, Web Usage, Infographic, Miscellaneous Natural Scenes). Stage 3: MTurk workers verified correctness of each annotated sample; 96% were found correct. Incorrect samples were filtered out, and each author group reviewed samples created by the other group to ensure guideline adherence and filter low-quality samples. Final dataset contains 506 instances.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three-stage annotation process: Stage 1 involved image shortlisting and filtering. Stage 2 involved authors divided into two groups, each annotating four specific categories, strictly following provided annotation guidelines to create image-instruction-response triplets requiring context-sensitive reasoning. Instructions include both questions and imperative tasks of varied complexity (extractive and reasoning-based). Stage 3 involved Amazon Mechanical Turk workers (mutually exclusive from those used for human performance baseline and human evaluation) verifying correctness of each sample; 96% were annotated correctly. Each author group then reviewed the other group's samples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (for verification in Stage 3, human performance baseline collection, and human evaluation)
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: MTurk workers verified 96% of samples as correctly annotated. Incorrect samples were filtered out. For human evaluation, each model response was shown to three human annotators independently, and the majority vote among the three annotators was used as the final decision on whether a predicted response was acceptable.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 (three human annotators independently rated each model response during human evaluation; majority vote used as final decision)
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Human annotators sourced mainly from the US via Amazon Mechanical Turk. Annotators who passed a qualification test were selected for the human performance baseline task.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: PaddleOCR (PP-OCRv4 model of PaddleOCR library) for OCR-based image filtering and text extraction; CLIP-retrieval UI for keyword-based image search from LAION-5B; ShareGPT-4V-7B for dense image captions in augmented LLM experiments; GPT-4 and GPT-4V for automatic evaluation of model responses.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: A subset of 100 samples (validation set) with reference responses will be released publicly, while reference responses for the remaining 406 samples will be kept hidden. The dataset is accompanied by a continuously updated leaderboard on HuggingFace. Dataset available on Hugging Face; code on GitHub.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset aims to ensure images, instructions, and responses are not offensive to any social group. Human annotators were mainly from the US, and the authors acknowledge that linguistic diversity and writing style of human responses would vary across different social groups.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: CONTEXTUAL is proposed to evaluate context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning capabilities of large multimodal models, with applications including assisting the visually impaired in interpreting text-rich scenes (e.g., navigating maps in public spaces) and creative understanding of abstract text-rich images (e.g., memes). The authors are aware that existing multimodal models can generate harmful responses despite safeguard filters, and note that model responses may hallucinate, though no apparent harmful or privacy-sensitive information was observed in qualitative analysis.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Human annotators for the baseline were mainly from the US, introducing potential linguistic and cultural bias. The authors acknowledge that linguistic diversity and writing style of human responses would change with different social groups, and that future work should involve annotators from more diverse regions. Open models may underperform on digital scenes due to training data predominantly comprising natural scenes (e.g., COCO dataset).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset contains 506 instances, which may limit statistical power for some fine-grained analyses. Human performance baseline was established mainly with US-based annotators, limiting generalizability across social groups. The dataset focuses on English-language instructions and responses. Automatic evaluation metrics (BLEURT, Rouge-L, BERTScore) show poor correlation with human judgments compared to GPT-4-based evaluation. Creating synthetic data for context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning is challenging, as automatic generation tends to produce instructions solvable by OCR+LLM.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluation of large multimodal models on context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning. The dataset is intended for testing/evaluation purposes. A validation set of 100 samples is released for model development, while the remaining 406 samples are held out for leaderboard evaluation. The dataset supports fine-grained analysis across eight visual scenarios and two task types (extractive reasoning and mathematical reasoning).
